correctness.rationale: Character diagonalization reduces exact complex nullity to zeros of \(T_\chi\). The index-three H fibers of \(f(u)=u+u^{k+1}\) are exactly \(h/2,-\omega h,-\omega^2h\). Cyclotomic field disjointness proves the common Gauss-period sum is never zero. The remaining factor vanishes iff \(\chi(-2)=1\) and \(\chi(\omega)\ne1\). Since \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-2)\) divides \(|H|\) and 3 is coprime to \(|H|\), annihilator counting gives precisely \(2(p-1)/(3\operatorname{ord}_p(-2))\) null modes, with explicit basis. A standalone checker independently verified all fibers and character counts for 13 admissible primes and numerical ranks for \(\(p=31,43\)\). Experiments are not used to establish unbounded prime quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Within inspected published and indexed results, closest prime-field hyperbola results establish only a \(d=1\) two-fiber quadratic obstruction, and parabola results concern a different quadratic phase. The cubic three-to-one phase geometry and order-sensitive kernel count do not follow from their statements. Earlier binomial and multiplicative Kloosterman literature provides ingredients, but not this Fourier-rank classification. Priority remains best-knowledge, with explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: Broad, mostly inaccessible 2021 arithmetic-Fourier work could imply related general rank identities; its abstract alone is not enough to establish noncoverage.
The full historical binomial-value-set, monomial-curve and twisted character-sum literature has not been exhaustively indexed; equivalent formulations could predate these sources.
The result does not prove infinitely many primes satisfy the cubic-resonance assumptions.

value.rationale: This is a motivated algebraic Fourier-recovery boundary: a family of nondegenerate reciprocal-power curves supports exactly calculable high-dimensional invisible sampling modes, unlike the at-most-one-dimensional quadratic obstruction of ordinary reciprocal hyperbolas. The answer is sharp, self-contained, valid for every prime satisfying a natural cubic-index subgroup condition, and supplies every missing character. Its exact order-dependent rank can inform finite-field sampling and spectral reconstruction even without a general inverse bound.
